editorial.headline: Metallurgical Machinery, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28230 covers machinery for hot metalworking, smelting, rolling, and related metallurgical or foundry equipment, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28230 is the manufacturing line for machinery used where metal is worked, melted, poured, or rolled. The record describes equipment for hot metalworking, including converters, steel ingot moulds, and ladling or pouring equipment used in metallurgy or metal casting. It also includes smelting machinery, metal rolling mills, rollers for similar mills, and machines for rolling metal in both hot and cold processes. In plain English, this is not the making of metal products themselves; it is the making of the machines that industrial metalworking depends on.

The activity is open across the full business-scale range recorded for this code: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the classification is not framed only for a large industrial actor in the record. A founder choosing this code would be describing the manufacture of metallurgical machinery and its equipment, whether the registered scale is small or large. The scope is technical, but it is also quite bounded: it is about machinery for hot metalworking, smelting, rolling, and metallurgical or foundry use, not every tool or mould connected with metal.

Nationally, the PMA picture is clean. The slim record marks the code as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In practical editorial terms, the foreign-ownership ceiling in the record is therefore 100%. There is no basis here to add another threshold, licence condition, capital figure, or timing requirement. The national message is simply that the code is open to foreign investment up to the recorded ceiling.

The Bali picture is also unusually straightforward. The record does include the Bali moratorium rule: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. But this specific record is not blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, l4_bali_blocked is false, and the stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. So the honest conclusion is not a hidden Bali cap or a local quota; it is that this code is nationally open, and the record does not mark it as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
